headline: An AI chip surge sparked by Meta's Muse assistant drove the Nasdaq to a record close and pushed AMD past a 1 trillion dollar valuation, while crude oil below 100 dollars lifted risk assets from equities to Bitcoin.

summary.us: Wall Street rallied on Monday 21 September as an AI chip surge lifted the Nasdaq Composite 2.26 percent to a record 27,122 and the S&P 500 gained 1.49 percent, with Intel up 12 percent, AMD up about 10 percent to a 1 trillion dollar market value, and Meta up 11 percent after its Muse AI assistant topped the App Store. Falling crude and a 10 year Treasury yield easing toward 4.96 percent added to the risk on tone.
summary.india: Indian equities were mixed at Monday's close, with the Nifty 50 up 0.29 percent and Bank Nifty up 0.20 percent as HDFC Bank rose on CEO succession news while TCS fell 3.9 percent and Infosys slipped, both IT majors now down more than a third in 2026. FIIs were net sellers of about 576 crore rupees in the cash segment against DII buying of about 2,797 crore, and the rupee held near 95.8 per dollar.
summary.global: Asia was firmer, with the Hang Seng up 1.18 percent and Shanghai higher ahead of a possible Trump Xi meeting, while Tokyo was closed for a holiday leaving the Nikkei at Friday's 1.38 percent gain and Europe was mixed. Brent slid below 100 dollars and WTI dropped more than 7 percent after President Trump signaled openness to diplomacy with Iran, while Bitcoin pushed back above 85,000 dollars, gold held near 4,390, and the dollar index steadied around 100.4.

weekly.narrative: The week belonged to central banks. The Federal Reserve raised rates a quarter point on 16 September to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first hike since 2023, and the Bank of Japan followed on 18 September with a split 7 to 2 vote that lifted its policy rate to a 31 year high of 1.25 percent, yet the yen weakened past 156 per dollar because two board members dissented and Governor Ueda made no commitment to further moves. US equities finished mixed as the 10 year Treasury yield came back to about 5 percent after touching a 19 year high above 5.04 percent ahead of the Fed, with the Dow down 1.69 percent on the week while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.72 percent. India was the weak spot, where the Nifty and Sensex logged a sixth consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing run in six years, under crude above 100 dollars, tighter global policy and a deepening Tata Sons governance dispute. Metals held their ground, with copper up about 2 percent on the week as the Yangshan import premium climbed 72 percent in September to a near four year high and silver adding 3.46 percent, while crypto turned sharply higher into the weekend on post Fed relief and rotation into altcoins. Next week brings S&P Global flash PMIs on 23 September, a heavy run of Fed speakers, Costco and Nike earnings on 24 September, and in India the Varmora Granito, Elevate Campuses, ArMee Infotech and A-One Steels offers alongside the close of the NSE IPO on 21 September.
